dedupe_keys.name: jarw refrigerated warehouse statistics japan monthly capacity inflows outflows and stocks of cold stores in 12 major cities and cold storage capacity by prefecture and temperature class

description: These statistics describe the stock of commercial cold stores that hold Japan's frozen and chilled fish, meat, vegetables and prepared food, and how full they are month by month. They are published by the Japan Association of Refrigerated Warehouses (JARW), the industry body of cold storage operators. Monthly tables for twelve major cities give the number of facilities, capacity in cubic metres, inflows, outflows, month-end and average stocks in tonnes, occupancy and turnover, with breakdowns by product group and comparisons with the previous month and year. A half-yearly list gives, for every prefecture, the capacity and number of member facilities in each temperature class from chilled to ultra-low temperature, and ice making and freezing capacity. The tables are free and available to download as PDF, with an archive back to 2006. Caveats: only JARW member facilities are counted, tables are PDFs, not data files, and the site states that all rights are reserved. Simulation uses: sizing cold chain storage capacity and buffer stocks in food supply models, testing the effect of a power cut or earthquake that disables cold stores in a port city, and tracking seasonal stock levels. Related records: the US cold storage report (data-usda-nass-cold-storage) is a comparable national series.

schema_summary: 12-city monthly tables (Sapporo, Sendai, Funabashi and other major cities): number of facilities, capacity (m3), usable capacity, inflow, outflow, month-end and average stock (tonnes), stock rate, occupancy rate, turnover, with ratios to the previous month and year; inflow, outflow and stock by product group; cumulative year-to-date tables; trend graphs. Prefecture tables (members' commercial cold stores): capacity and number of facilities by temperature class (F1 to F3, SF1 to SF4, C1 to C3), ice making and freezing capacity (t/day), change from the previous period
